introduction: Pure metals are often too soft or easily rusted to be used practically. To improve their properties (like hardness or rust resistance), they are mixed with other elements to form Alloys.

core_concepts.title: Alloy
core_concepts.description: A 'homogeneous mixture' of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal). It is prepared by melting the primary metal and then dissolving the other elements in it.

core_concepts.title: Important Alloys and their Composition
core_concepts.description:
1. Brass: Copper (Cu) + Zinc (Zn). Uses: Utensils, decorative items. 
2. Bronze: Copper (Cu) + Tin (Sn). Uses: Statues, Bronze medals, coins. 
3. Solder: Lead (Pb) + Tin (Sn). Uses: Welding electrical wires (has a very low melting point). 
4. Stainless Steel: Iron (Fe) + Chromium (Cr) + Nickel (Ni) + Carbon (C). Uses: Surgical instruments, utensils (it does not rust).

core_concepts.title: Amalgam
core_concepts.description: If one of the metals in an alloy is 'Mercury (Hg)', then the alloy is known as an Amalgam. (For example, Silver-Tin amalgam is used by dentists to fill tooth cavities).

core_concepts.title: Corrosion and Prevention
core_concepts.description:
The gradual destruction of metals by the action of air (oxygen) and moisture. 
- Rusting of Iron: Forms a reddish-brown flaky coating ($Fe_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O$). 
- Copper: Develops a 'Green' coating (due to Copper Carbonate). 
- Silver: Develops a 'Black' coating (due to Silver Sulfide).

important_entities.name: Galvanization
important_entities.significance: Galvanization is the process of coating iron or steel objects with a thin layer of 'Zinc (Zn)' to protect them from rusting. Because zinc is more reactive than iron, it sacrifices itself to protect the iron underneath.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Ultimate Exam Trap: 'Which metal does NOT form an amalgam with Mercury?' The answer is 'Iron (Fe), Platinum, and Tungsten'. This is exactly why liquid Mercury is safely stored and transported in 'Iron flasks'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: BraSS has an 'S', so it does NOT use Tin (Sn); it uses Zinc (Zn). BronZe has a 'Z', so it does NOT use Zinc; it uses Tin (Sn). They are opposite to their spellings!

exam_strategy_tips: Frequently asked in NDA/CDS: 'The solder used for welding electrical wires is an alloy of?' Answer: Lead and Tin.
